# Are co-accessible pairs driven by haplotype differences (Hapolotype Specific Chromatin Accessibility - HSCA)?

A pooled 2x2 table mixes the two haplotypes of every sample. When both cCREs are more open on
the same haplotype the odds ratio is inflated; when they are open on opposite haplotypes it is
deflate
- Haplotype-selective chromatin accessibility (HSCA) can come from imprinting, cis variants (HSCA-withVar) and clonal somatic epimutations (HSCA-noVar) (Vollger et al., Cell 2026).

The test is the paper's: two-sided Fisher on accessible vs not accessible fibers per haplotype, BH, FDR <= 0.05, at least 10 reads per haplotype. Applied to a pair, "accessible" becomes "both cCREs open" on reads that span both cCREs

| Unit | Within sample, H1 vs H2 | Within sample, REF vs ALT | Across samples, REF vs ALT |
|---|---|---|---|
| cCRE | `LCL_hsca_cre_status` | `LCL_hsca_cre_allele_by_sample` | `LCL_hsca_cre_allele` |
| pair | `LCL_hsca_pair_status` | `LCL_hsca_pair_allele_by_sample` | `LCL_hsca_pair_allele` |

- `LCL_hsca_cre_status`: FIRE's own per-peak hap1 vs hap2 test (`<sample>-fire-v0.1-hap-differences.bed.gz`)
  intersected with the paired cCREs; status hap1 / hap2 / conflict / ns; a missing row = untested.
  
- H1/H2 are each sample's HiPhase tags: they are only compared within one sample and one phase
  block (pairs use the reads of their majority block).

- A skew that follows the allele across samples is genetic; a within-sample skew without a
  consistent allele (or without a het SNV) is an imprinting or epimutation candidate



```bash
cd /project/spott/cshan/fiber-seq/code/co-accessibility/LCL/hsca
sbatch LCL_run_hsca.sh   # -> LCL_project/co-accessibility/hsca/outputs/
```

the imprinted differentially mwthylated regions (DMRs), is used as known imprinted regions from - Akbari V, Garant J-M, O’Neill K, Pandoh P, Moore R, Marra MA, Hirst M, Jones SJM (2022). “Genome-wide detection of imprinted differentially methylated regions using nanopore sequencing.” eLife 11:e77898.


the analysis was done on 27 phased samples: /project/spott/1_Shared_projects/LCL_Fiber_seq/Data/LCL_sample_metatable_merged_samples_27samples.csv



1. Identify skewed CRE pairs
  - at least 10 reads in each group (hap1 vs hap2 within a sample, ref vs alt after pooling all samples)
  
  - A two-sided Fisher exact test compares the fraction of reads that are open between the two groups. For H1 vs H2 on a cCRE, “open” means the cCRE is accessible. For a pair, “open” means both cCREs are open on the same read.
    - For REF vs ALT, the reads are split by the base at the chosen het SNV.
    - BH correction is applied within each sample.
    - The unit is skewed if the adjusted p-value is ≤ 0.05
    - The sign of diff (group 1 open fraction minus group 2 open fraction) sets the label: hap1 or hap2 for the haplotype tests. alt or ref for the allele tests.

## Tested and skewed per sample

```{r sample-tallies}
tally = function(dt, name) {
  dt[, .(tested = .N, skewed = sum(status != "ns")), by = sample_name][
    , setnames(.SD, c("tested", "skewed"), paste0(name, c("_tested", "_skewed")))]
}

sample_tallies = Reduce(function(a, b) merge(a, b, by = "sample_name", all = TRUE), list(
  tally(cre_status, "cre_hap"),
  cre_status[, .(cre_hap_conflict = sum(status == "conflict")), by = sample_name],
  tally(pair_status, "pair_hap"),
  tally(cre_allele_by_sample, "cre_allele"),
  tally(pair_allele_by_sample, "pair_allele")))
for (j in setdiff(names(sample_tallies), "sample_name")) set(sample_tallies, which(is.na(sample_tallies[[j]])), j, 0L)
fwrite(sample_tallies, file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_sample_tallies.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(sample_tallies)

pooled_tallies = data.table(
  table = c("LCL_hsca_cre_allele", "LCL_hsca_pair_allele"),
  with_variant = c(nrow(cre_allele), nrow(pair_allele)),
  tested = c(sum(!is.na(cre_allele$p_value)), sum(!is.na(pair_allele$p_value))),
  fdr_lt_0.05 = c(sum(cre_allele$fdr < fdr_cut, na.rm = TRUE), sum(pair_allele$fdr < fdr_cut, na.rm = TRUE)))
knitr::kable(pooled_tallies)
```

## Are pooled co-accessible pairs haplotype- or allele-skewed?

Pooled positives are `fdr < 0.05 & OR > 1 & co_access > expected_co_access` in the pooled table (all chromosomes) and the noXCI table; only autosomal pairs can be tested here
Each test compares the skewed fraction of positives with the skewed fraction of the other tested pairs.

```{r pooled-positive-enrichment}
positives = list(
  all_chr = pooled[fdr < fdr_cut & OR > 1 & co_access > expected_co_access, CRE_pair],
  noXCI = pooled_noxci[fdr_noXCI < fdr_cut & OR_noXCI > 1 & co_access_noXCI > expected_co_access_noXCI, CRE_pair])

# per pair: tested / skewed by haplotype (within sample) and by allele (within sample or pooled)
pair_flags = merge(
  pair_status[, .(hap_skewed = any(status != "ns")), by = CRE_pair],
  rbind(pair_allele_by_sample[, .(CRE_pair, skewed = status != "ns")],
        pair_allele[!is.na(p_value), .(CRE_pair, skewed = fdr < fdr_cut)])[, .(allele_skewed = any(skewed)), by = CRE_pair],
  by = "CRE_pair", all = TRUE)

enrichment = rbindlist(lapply(names(positives), function(set) {
  rbindlist(lapply(c("hap_skewed", "allele_skewed"), function(test) {
    d = pair_flags[!is.na(get(test)), .(positive = CRE_pair %in% positives[[set]], skewed = get(test))]
    ft = fisher.test(table(factor(d$positive, c(TRUE, FALSE)), factor(d$skewed, c(TRUE, FALSE))))
    data.table(positive_set = set, test = test, n_tested = nrow(d), n_positive_tested = sum(d$positive),
               n_skewed = sum(d$skewed), n_positive_skewed = sum(d$positive & d$skewed),
               frac_skewed_positive = mean(d$skewed[d$positive]), frac_skewed_other = mean(d$skewed[!d$positive]),
               odds_ratio = unname(ft$estimate), p_value = ft$p.value)
  }))
}))
fwrite(enrichment, file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_pooled_positive_enrichment.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(enrichment, digits = 4)
```

## Co-accessible pairs with pooled allele selectivity, ranked by p-value

These lists use the **pooled REF/ALT pair test**, not the within-sample H1/H2 test.
Co-accessibility still requires pooled co-accessibility FDR < 0.05, OR > 1, and observed
both-open counts above expectation. Within that set, raw allele p < 0.05 identifies
**exploratory candidates**; allele BH FDR < 0.05 identifies the corrected discoveries.
The allele BH values are retained from the original test across all tested autosomal pairs;
they are **not recalculated after selecting co-accessible pairs**. Every list is sorted by
raw allele p-value, with CRE_pair breaking ties. Coordinates are BED (0-based, end-exclusive).
The `difference_pp` column is ALT minus REF both-open fraction, in percentage points.

```{r ranked-allele-pairs}
pair_annotation = pooled[, .(CRE_pair, chrom, cre1_start, cre1_end, cre2_start, cre2_end,
  gene_names, CRE_pair_labels, coaccess_OR = OR, coaccess_fdr = fdr,
  coaccess_p_value = pval, n_shared_reads, co_access, expected_co_access)]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(pair_annotation$CRE_pair), !anyDuplicated(pair_allele$CRE_pair))
ranked_pair_alleles = merge(copy(pair_allele[!is.na(p_value)]), pair_annotation,
  by = "CRE_pair", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
stopifnot(!anyNA(ranked_pair_alleles$chrom))
setnames(ranked_pair_alleles, c("p_value", "fdr"), c("allele_p_value", "allele_bh_fdr"))
ranked_pair_alleles[, `:=`(
  coaccessible = CRE_pair %in% positives$all_chr,
  allele_nominal = allele_p_value < fdr_cut,
  allele_bh_significant = allele_bh_fdr < fdr_cut,
  ref_n = ref_open + ref_closed,
  alt_n = alt_open + alt_closed,
  difference_percentage_points = 100 * diff)]
setorder(ranked_pair_alleles, allele_p_value, CRE_pair)
rank_pair_list = function(d) {
  d = copy(d)
  d[, rank := seq_len(.N)]
  setcolorder(d, c("rank", setdiff(names(d), "rank")))
  d[]
}
coaccessible_allele_nominal = rank_pair_list(ranked_pair_alleles[coaccessible & allele_nominal])
coaccessible_allele_bh = rank_pair_list(ranked_pair_alleles[coaccessible & allele_bh_significant])
all_pair_allele_bh = rank_pair_list(ranked_pair_alleles[allele_bh_significant == TRUE])
fwrite(coaccessible_allele_nominal,
  file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_coaccessible_pair_allele_nominal_ranked.tsv"), sep = "\t")
fwrite(coaccessible_allele_bh,
  file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_coaccessible_pair_allele_BH_ranked.tsv"), sep = "\t")
fwrite(all_pair_allele_bh,
  file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_all_pair_allele_BH_ranked.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(data.table(
  group = c("Co-accessible pairs with an allele test", "Raw allele p < 0.05 (exploratory)",
            "Allele BH FDR < 0.05 among co-accessible pairs", "Allele BH FDR < 0.05 among all pairs"),
  n_pairs = c(sum(ranked_pair_alleles$coaccessible), nrow(coaccessible_allele_nominal),
              nrow(coaccessible_allele_bh), nrow(all_pair_allele_bh))))

# Show every passing pair; scientific notation keeps small p-values visible.
show_ranked_pairs = function(d) {
  knitr::kable(d[, .(rank, CRE_pair, gene_names,
    CRE1_interval = paste0(chrom, ":", cre1_start, "-", cre1_end),
    CRE2_interval = paste0(chrom, ":", cre2_start, "-", cre2_end), variant_id,
    REF_both_open = paste0(ref_open, "/", ref_n),
    ALT_both_open = paste0(alt_open, "/", alt_n),
    difference_pp = round(difference_percentage_points, 2),
    allele_p = formatC(allele_p_value, format = "e", digits = 3),
    allele_BH_FDR = formatC(allele_bh_fdr, format = "e", digits = 3),
    coaccess_FDR = formatC(coaccess_fdr, format = "e", digits = 3),
    coaccessible, n_samples_both_alleles)])
}
```

## Reusable CRE-pair plotting

`plot_cre_pair(cre_pair)` prepares the reads and writes the plots for one pair:
phased molecule tracks, phased configuration bars, the unclustered phased-molecule heatmap, the
Manhattan/Leiden heatmap, cluster m6A profiles, neighbor graphs and allele composition,
plus autocorrelation heatmaps, profiles, and clustering. Only PDFs are written to the
example folders; read labels, phasing audits, assignments, and profiles remain in the
returned R object.
The input can be a full `CRE_pair` string from the ranked table or a vector of two full
CRE IDs. Coordinates and the focal SNP come from the pooled and allele-test tables.
The pair must have an allele-test SNV and enough fully spanning, phaseable molecules
for the existing phasing filter (at least three reads and both SNP alleles).

Output filenames default to both CRE accessions, so pairs near the same gene remain
separate. `label` sets the gene label for titles and folders (by default, gene symbols
from the pair annotation); `output_prefix` optionally chooses a filename stem.
`region_description` adds positional context, for example `"upstream of PTGER4"`.
Future plot titles include this description and the full plotted window's hg38 coordinates
(1-based, inclusive). If no description is supplied, a neutral gene-locus label is used;
upstream/downstream relationships are not inferred from proximity alone.
Each pair gets a directory named with its gene label and both CRE accessions under `CRE_pairs_examples/`,
containing only its PDFs. `output_dir` overrides the parent directory. The function returns the
plot objects, underlying data, output directory, and PDF paths.
It preserves the original full-span filters, yellow CRE bands, SNP markers, REF/ALT
legends, and clustering settings. It does not change the allele tests or BH values.

For another pair, after running the notebook setup and function definitions:

```r
cxcr4_id = coaccessible_allele_nominal[rank == 14L, CRE_pair]
cxcr4_plots = plot_cre_pair(cxcr4_id, label = "CXCR4")
cxcr4_plots$files
# For several selected pairs, call the same function once per pair:
# lapply(selected_pair_ids, plot_cre_pair)
```

The same function and read filters generate all PDFs for each pair, in separate
pair directories under `CRE_pairs_examples/`. The phased tracks and clustered heatmaps
are also displayed here; configuration bars, profiles, and neighbor graphs are in the PDFs.


```{r example-pair-summary, echo=FALSE}
if (isTRUE(params$make_molecule_plots)) {
  example_results = list(SLFN5 = slfn5, TNFAIP3 = tnfaip3, FAS = fas)
  example_summary = rbindlist(lapply(names(example_results), function(gene) {
    x = example_results[[gene]]
    data.table(gene = gene, CRE_pair = x$pair_id,
      phased_track_molecules = nrow(x$read_labels),
      phased_heatmap_molecules = nrow(x$phased_molecules$assignments),
      input_full_window_molecules = x$phased_molecules$params$n_input_full_window,
      unassigned_excluded = x$phased_molecules$params$n_unassigned_excluded,
      samples = uniqueN(x$phased_molecules$assignments$sample_name),
      Leiden_clusters = x$phased_molecules$n_clusters,
      REF_molecules = sum(x$phased_molecules$assignments$allele_group == paste0("REF-", x$region$ref)),
      ALT_molecules = sum(x$phased_molecules$assignments$allele_group == paste0("ALT-", x$region$alt)),
      ACF_clusters = x$autocorrelation$result$n_clusters,
      ACF_molecules = nrow(x$autocorrelation$result$assignments), output_dir = x$output_dir)
  }))
  knitr::kable(example_summary[, !"output_dir"])
}
```

## PTGER4 and WDFY4: upstream CRE-pair examples

Rank 19 is the pair upstream of PTGER4, and rank 30 is upstream of WDFY4 in the
nominal-p ranked list. These are positional labels, not evidence that either pair
regulates the named gene. Both pairs are upstream of the plus-strand canonical TSS
in `/project/spott/cshan/annotations/gencodev46_Ensembl_canonical_TSS.bed`:
PTGER4 at chr5:40,679,915 and WDFY4 at chr10:48,684,873 (hg38, 1-based).
The titles give the plotted windows, including the flanks. Only these new examples
need to be executed to add their PDFs; existing example PDFs need not be regenerated.

## Gene, domain and CTCF context of the CRE-pair examples

One PDF per pair in `CRE_domain_CTCF_anno/`. The top block is the locus context: canonical
GENCODE v46 transcripts, Rao et al. 2014 GM12878 HiCCUPS loops and Arrowhead domains, lifted
hg19 -> hg38 by `rao2014_GM12878/liftover_to_hg38.sh`. Loops are arcs between anchor midpoints:
loops with an anchor in the pair window are red and labelled, with CTCF motif arrows at their
anchors. Domains are triangles. The yellow band is the pair window (pair +/- `locus_flank_bp`),
which the bottom block shows at base resolution. That block has transcript structure, loop
anchors, motifs and domain edges in the window, the cCREs, per-base m6A by genotype group
(fraction of the group's molecules with a call; no smoothing) and every molecule's m6A.

Genotypes come from each sample's reads at the focal SNV: the base each primary read carries,
the rule of the pooled allele test. They do not come from the VCFs, so homozygous donors, the four
samples without a VCF and the samples carrying another person's VCF genotypes are all labelled
from their own reads. A sample needs at least 5 informative reads. It is het when the minor
allele has at least 2 reads and at least 15% of them, and otherwise homozygous for the majority
allele. Het donors' molecules are split by their own base. Molecules are the full-window primary
alignments that cover both cCREs, from all 31 samples: the molecule-track read rule without its
phasing requirement. The pooled 2x2 is reproduced as a check. There is no clustering. These
figures do not change the allele tests or BH values.

```{r domain-ctcf-data, include=FALSE}
if (isTRUE(params$make_molecule_plots)) {
  gene_models = load_canonical_gene_models("/project/spott/cshan/annotations/gencode.v46.annotation.gtf.gz")
  rao_hg38 = load_rao_hg38("/project/spott/cshan/annotations/LCL_public_data/rao2014_GM12878/hg38")
}
```

```{r domain-ctcf-examples, include=FALSE}
domain_ctcf = NULL
if (isTRUE(params$make_molecule_plots)) {
  domain_ctcf = list(
    SLFN5 = plot_cre_pair_domain_ctcf(
      c("EH38D5005816.EH38E3219251.PLS", "EH38D6268395.EH38E4160235.pELS"), "SLFN5"),
    TNFAIP3 = plot_cre_pair_domain_ctcf(
      c("EH38D5796985.EH38E3735644.dELS", "EH38D3906538.EH38E2507553.dELS"), "TNFAIP3"),
    FAS = plot_cre_pair_domain_ctcf(
      c("EH38D2372847.EH38E1486833.pELS", "EH38D4537003.EH38E2915259.PLS"), "FAS"),
    PTGER4 = plot_cre_pair_domain_ctcf(
      c("EH38D3696628.EH38E2368242.dELS", "EH38D5644181.EH38E3633999.pELS"), "PTGER4",
      region_description = "upstream of PTGER4"),
    WDFY4 = plot_cre_pair_domain_ctcf(
      c("EH38D6178319.EH38E4008375.dELS", "EH38D6178323.EH38E4008379.PLS"), "WDFY4",
      region_description = "upstream of WDFY4"))
}
```

```{r domain-ctcf-group-sizes, echo=FALSE}
  domain_ctcf[[gene]]$group_sizes[, .(gene, focal_snv = domain_ctcf[[gene]]$allele$variant_id,
    group = cluster, molecules, samples, donors)])))
```

## Haplotype-skewed pairs: are both cCREs selective on the same haplotype?

For each pair skewed within a sample, the FIRE hap1/hap2 status of CRE1 and CRE2 in the same
sample. Directions are compared only when both cCREs lie inside one HiPhase block of that sample
(`cres_same_block`). "same haplotype" is the case that inflates a pooled odds ratio and "opposite
haplotypes" the case that deflates it.

```{r skewed-pair-directions}
cre_calls = cre_status[, .(sample_name, CRE_ID, status)]
skewed_pairs = pair_status[status != "ns"]
skewed_pairs = merge(skewed_pairs, setnames(copy(cre_calls), c("CRE_ID", "status"), c("CRE1", "cre1_status")),
                     by = c("sample_name", "CRE1"), all.x = TRUE)
skewed_pairs = merge(skewed_pairs, setnames(copy(cre_calls), c("CRE_ID", "status"), c("CRE2", "cre2_status")),
                     by = c("sample_name", "CRE2"), all.x = TRUE)
skewed_pairs[, category := fcase(
  !cres_same_block, "not comparable (different blocks)",
  cre1_status %in% "conflict" | cre2_status %in% "conflict", "conflict",
  cre1_status %in% hap_status & cre2_status %in% hap_status & cre1_status == cre2_status, "same haplotype",
  cre1_status %in% hap_status & cre2_status %in% hap_status, "opposite haplotypes",
  cre1_status %in% hap_status | cre2_status %in% hap_status, "one cCRE only",
  cre1_status %in% "ns" & cre2_status %in% "ns", "neither (both ns)",
  default = "untested")]
skewed_pairs[, `:=`(pooled_positive = CRE_pair %in% positives$all_chr, noXCI_positive = CRE_pair %in% positives$noXCI)]
direction_summary = skewed_pairs[, .(n = .N, n_pooled_positive = sum(pooled_positive),
                                     n_noXCI_positive = sum(noXCI_positive)), by = category][order(-n)]
fwrite(direction_summary, file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_skewed_pair_directions.tsv"), sep = "\t")
fwrite(skewed_pairs[order(sample_name, p_adjust)], file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_skewed_pairs.tsv.gz"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(direction_summary)
```

## cCREs with haplotype-selective accessibility: genetic, imprinted or epimutation?

Every cCRE that is hap1, hap2 or conflict in at least one sample, classified by the pooled REF/ALT
test at its het SNV:

- imprinted: overlaps an Akbari DMR (REF/ALT pooling cannot detect parent-of-origin effects)
- allele-associated (genetic): pooled REF vs ALT fdr < 0.05
- no allele association (epimutation candidate): het SNV tested, pooled fdr >= 0.05
- allele not testable: het SNV without reads on both alleles
- no het SNV (noVar): no het SNV inside the cCRE in any of the 27 phased samples

```{r hsca-cre-classes}
hsca_cres = cre_status[status %in% c(hap_status, "conflict"), .(n_hsca_samples = uniqueN(sample_name),
                                                              hsca_samples = paste(sort(unique(sample_name)), collapse = ";")), by = CRE_ID]
hsca_cres = merge(hsca_cres, cre_allele[, .(CRE_ID, variant_id, n_het_samples, diff, p_value, fdr,
                                             n_samples_alt_higher, n_samples_ref_higher, n_samples_both_alleles)],
                  by = "CRE_ID", all.x = TRUE)
hsca_cres[, class := fcase(
  CRE_ID %in% imprinted_cres, "imprinted",
  is.na(variant_id), "no het SNV (noVar)",
  is.na(fdr), "allele not testable",
  fdr < fdr_cut, "allele-associated (genetic)",
  default = "no allele association (epimutation candidate)")]
class_summary = hsca_cres[, .(n_cres = .N, median_hsca_samples = median(n_hsca_samples)), by = class][order(-n_cres)]
fwrite(hsca_cres[order(class, fdr)], file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_cre_classes.tsv"), sep = "\t")
fwrite(class_summary, file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_cre_class_summary.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(class_summary)
```
